surface._comment: Road-surface LINE layer (Dated/2026-08-09-surface-line-tiles-design.md, owner-approved 2026-08-10). Zero DB rows: ways stream straight to GeoJSONL and tippecanoe. The seven class names are the client's SURFACE_STYLE keys and are pinned to it by a cross-language test. | minZoom was 8 until 2026-08-20. The build runs with --no-tile-size-limit, so a low-zoom tile carries every classified way under it instead of a sampled 500 KB: measured over Wallonia one tile was 1119 KB at z8 and 455 KB at z9 against 93 KB at z10, and a screen is roughly sixteen tiles at any zoom, which made a default region view about 16 MB. Nothing legible was lost at those zooms either - the client paints this layer 0.6 px wide at half opacity at z8. The client carries the same floor as CLASSIFIED_MIN_ZOOM and a cross-language test pins the two together; the planning-zoom question is answered by the gaps grid, which is built z4-11 for exactly that reason.

todo._comment: The "needs a tag" arm is NOT every untagged way — it is the ways whose answer is genuinely unknown. Measured on Belgium's tagged ways (2026-08-12): a primary road is unpaved 0.1% of the time, secondary 0.5%, tertiary 2.5%, cycleway 0.0%, residential 7.2% — and since mappers tag the surprising road first, an UNTAGGED one of those classes is safer still. Asking a rider to go and record them is asking them to confirm asphalt. Tracks (88% unpaved), paths (50/50) and rural unclassified lanes (6.8%) are where nobody can predict the answer, and they are a third of the bytes: 43.3 MB -> 16 MB for Belgium. | 2026-08-12: tertiary and cycleway were briefly added here and then withdrawn. The gap they were meant to fix (an untagged tertiary on a signed route, e.g. the Zuiderdijk) is real, but highway class is the wrong key for it: the rule that survives is ROUTE-AWARENESS — an untagged way carrying a signed route or node network is homework whatever its class, because a rider rides it BECAUSE it is signed. Implement with the routes extractor (docs/plans/handoffs/2026-08-12-routes-layer-and-surface-quality.md).

gaps._comment: The planning half of the same question. Per-cell km of unrecorded to-do network, so "where should I go scanning?" is answered by ~900 squares per country (0.5 MB for Belgium) instead of 400,000 line geometries. cellZoom 12 is ~6 km at 50N. maxZoom hands over to the to-do lines exactly where they begin (todo.minZoom), so one legend row means squares at planning zoom and roads at riding zoom.

quality._comment: Surface QUALITY as its own visual channel (owner 2026-08-12): we store smoothness and OSM carries the same vocabulary, but the tiles used to ship only cls/hw/ref, so good pavement and bone-shaking pave drew identically. `sm` carries the raw OSM smoothness value (this list, verbatim - an unlisted value is dropped, not guessed); `mtb` carries mtb:scale. The client draws short coloured ticks above minZoom, ONLY where sm is present - no ticks means nobody has said, the same honesty rule as the red dotted line. Pinned to the client's tone mapping by surface-quality.test.cjs.

surface._roadTypeChannel: Road type is NOT a colour in this scale (owner 2026-08-12). `highway=cycleway` used to override the surface class, which answered two questions with one key. The raw highway value rides every feature as `hw` (tileProps) and the client draws a cycleway as a pale core inside whatever surface colour it has.

routes._comment: Cycle-route NETWORK layer (docs/plans/handoffs/2026-08-12-routes-layer-and-surface-quality.md): route=bicycle and route=mtb relations, one line feature per MEMBER WAY plus knooppunt nodes as points. Rendering corridors is borrowed (OpenCycleMap is the benchmark, readable-by-default the brief); what the layer buys us is the loop with the surface skin - a signed way with no recorded surface is homework whatever its highway class, and the extractor's way-id set is what makes the surface to-do arm route-aware. `net` is the relation's network canonicalised to this list (route=mtb is always mtb; an unlisted network on route=bicycle is other); `ref` is the OSM ELEMENT ref (way/NNN - same key, same meaning as every other layer, the /improve and source-link join key); the ROUTE's code (LF-ZZ, 09-80) travels as `rr`; `rk` says route vs node-network segment; `refs` joins every membership when a way carries more than one. Node features ride the same artifact with a per-feature tippecanoe minzoom of nodes.minZoom.
routes._zoomComment: TWO FLOORS on one archive, the same trick the knooppunt nodes already use. `minZoom` is the ARCHIVE floor and is now 5, because an international route is a thing a rider plans at the zoom where a country fits on the screen - and below 8 the layer used to be simply absent, which reads as broken rather than as out of range (owner 2026-08-17). What keeps that from meaning 2.7 million local lines at z5 is `planningNetworks`: only those get the low floor, stamped per feature; everything else keeps `localMinZoom` and appears exactly where it always did. The client needs no zoom rule of its own - a network with no features in a z6 tile draws nothing.

nodes._comment: Knooppunten: nodes carrying rcn_ref/lcn_ref, emitted as points with their number in `nr`. minZoom keeps a country's thousands of numbers out of the low planning zooms; the client draws the badges from here up (routes-tiles.js, symbol collision culls what does not fit), and the two are pinned by routes-zooms.test.cjs. Lowered 11->10 on owner feedback 2026-08-13: the numbers are how riders plan, and z10 is where planning starts.
